subject: ADR-195: the report gets a `since` too -- the gap two of ADR-194's four operators reported independently, 15,337 bytes of stand-sheet report down to 101 when nothing moved and 1,712 when something did, and the wildcard the contract needed to do it
body: ADR-191 gave the SNAPSHOT a stamp and a diff and ADR-194 proved it -- all four operators took the ~100KB snapshot once and never again -- and then two of those four reported the same gap independently: THE DIFF IS CONTROL-SHAPED. A read-report is 30-100KB and is the document a science task is actually about, and it had no `since`, so an operator watching a computed figure re-read the whole report to learn one box moved (fourteen such calls on the stand sheet alone). read-report now carries a `stamp` and takes a `since`: 15,337 bytes -> 101 when nothing moved, 1,712 when something did, and the WHOLE report plus the reason for a stamp this session never issued -- failing toward more exactly as observe does, because a diff against a baseline that is not there would be invented. TWO DOCUMENTS, ONE ALGORITHM: REPORT_IDENTITY says what identity means on a report and the contract's own stamp_of/diff_of do the work; boxes are reported as THAT BOX changing with both sides trimmed, lines are named rather than counted, tables are NOT keyed because a row of cells has no identity of its own. THE ONE NEW THING IN THE CONTRACT is key_for(path, keys): a keyed path may carry a `*`, an exact path wins, a pattern matches segment for segment and length for length -- because a report's lists live under ids the PAGE chose and a spec that had to enumerate them would go stale the first time a page grew a box. Both stamp_of and diff_of go through it and the suite holds that they agree. The report's stamp and ADR-188's `version` are about different documents and both are published. verify_contract 143 -> 148, verify_report 179 -> 194, mutate_contract 60 -> 65, mutate_report 110 -> 118. No report's contents changed.
